The evidence chunks provided are essentially identical across all genes (all rated critic_relevance=2/5, none with direct gene-specific mentions). Since the literature evidence doesn't differentiate the genes, I must rely on prior knowledge about which gene is most plausibly causal for this phenotype profile.

The phenotype profile — conjugated hyperbilirubinemia, elevated bile acids, elevated AST/ALT, hepatosplenomegaly, pruritus, jaundice, growth delay, scoliosis, pointed helix — is highly consistent with Progressive Familial Intrahepatic Cholestasis (PFIC) or a related cholestatic liver disease. The "pointed helix" and "scoliosis" suggest a syndromic form. Among the candidate genes, none are canonical PFIC genes (ATP8B1, ABCB11, ABCB4), but FCSK has been associated with a congenital disorder of glycosylation with cholestatic liver disease. DPY19L3 has a chunk specifically describing a patient with persistent itching, elevated bile acids, direct hyperbilirubinemia, transaminitis, hepatosplenomegaly, and poor weight gain — matching this phenotype most closely. The CUX2 chunk also describes a cholestatic pattern. Given the DPY19L3 chunk most specifically describes a matching clinical scenario including splenomegaly and progressive cholestatic disease, it ranks highest.
